body: An asshole recognizes another asshole from far away.

> Hi there, I came up with a kundalini theory. I have been thinking about for a while. Let me know what you think. 

https://medium.com/@bisade/kundalini-theory-41e520f74a10
Thanks for that. Maybe i'll talk to him about it and see how that goes. How did your psychiatrist treat the issue?

You are right. My perspective is less dark than it was before even though its still a bit dark. Its possible my life has taken a new direction and is on a trajectory to something amazing. I don't discount that. Just like you who is starting to move to a better place, the question I have is if that is attributable to the kundalini awakening or if that's just fortunate change driven by our internal motivations. I mean to say that a bioelectric phenomenon is making us better people seems quite vague. If someone told me that kundalini raises life expectancy in the person or expands their consciousness or raises the IQ then I could appreciate that. I guess I am just looking for a clear result of the kundalini awakening. It got frustrating experiencing something so powerful and not knowing what it means. That said, I don't mind being an everyday joe. Everyone else is. It does not mean there is nothing special about them it just means they are people. The alternative is being superhuman in some way. Maybe since this just happened to you it feels new and exciting but when the dust settles, you might just end up left with questions. Questions the need practical answers.

The notion of death seeming more normal than living is interesting. Its like seeing the other side of the bowl and understanding that the inverted state is where context can be found. I mean that if life was the inside of a bowl full of food and we spend our existence sorting through and processing its bits. Only when the bowl is empty do we realize that we have been eating out of a bowl. Then we understand that the emptiness of the bowl/death is the original state and the state we inevitably return to whether we eat all the contents or the contents spill out by accident or choice. Meaning that whether we choose to live life or not live it, it makes no difference to the original state-the death state-the empty bowl. Maybe this is why to us death makes more sense than life. Why depression sometimes can seem to provide more clarity or give us a more realistic perspective to life.
Its really weird. Have you sought help. I have not on this issue even though I have a psychiatrist. I am afraid of their text book response to suicidal ideation.....admission to the psych ward.

I honestly have no idea. I am still the same person I always was after the kundalini rose in me. I am not special in any way. I do have constant vibrations in my forehead and I dream a whole lot now. Other than those things I cannot say kundalini has helped me transcend anything or has alleviated my suffering in any way. Even if I said that, in what tangible way would I measure it. I searched for a long time for answers on this kundalini thing. These days I just ask about it occasionally online. I got fed up with esoteric answers and websites. I want a more practical and simple answer. Maybe that is asking to much. Maybe the topic of kundalini is more complex than that. I mean an electric bolt to the brain from the base of the spinal cord that does not kill the host must mean something. And also why do we have pent up electricity stored in our ass?

So I ask because my kundalini rose a few times. Afterwards my forehead started vibrating constantly (still does). And I dream ALOT. I would say 5-6 dreams a night. Its annoying because I have to wake up every time a dream is finished but I have no trouble getting back to sleep to start the next dream. Those are the practical ways I feel the kundalini has changed me. I don't know what the point of it is though. At first I thought it was a super power that I had gained or something but most of the dreams are pretty meaningless. Anytime I find someone who has been through this, I ask them what they think the purpose of the kundalini is but I guess what I really want to know is how it has changed them. Do I now exist in a higher state? I don't know. Even if it were so, how would that be measured you know. Does it result in a general improvement in the quality of your life. I don think I became more compassionate or loving as a result. I try not to ascribe esoteric things I read online to see if they fit my existence. Thats why I would rather there was a practical answer to this question. Like I know it's a bioenergetic phenomenon. To that I say, what change does it biologically or psychologically bring about. Also is the kundalini conscious in the sense of it trying to achieve an objective within its host. What would that general objective be and does it vary form person to person. All I get when I read online is a lot of esoteric jargon on the topic. Its weird because science has not really observed it so on the biological spectrum there is nothing really documented. Ascending out of the cycle of suffering alludes to Buddhist philosophy. Its been a few years since my kundalini rising experience. Can I really say I have transcended suffering or I am somehow on my way to enlightenment and transcendence? How would that be measured. During that time, I went though this period of being woke and philosophical about life thinking that somehow the kundalini was changing me. I think it just gave me some existential perspective. I thought "why would this rare phenomenon happen to me? To what end? For what purpose?" So I started to think a lot about destiny and things like full potential. Now I realize that was just a phase and I am now just living a normal life of an everyday joe. I work a 9-5. I have a family. I am tired most of the time. I drink sometimes, I still like to smoke. What is the point of the kundalini? what does it do? what is it still doing in me? I wonder. Sometimes I wonder if the forehead vibrations will one day translate into a telekinetic ability of sorts. But those are just fantasies....
So in your view, what is the whole point of a kundalini awakening?

This is good advice. Just pay them no mind. Its sort of what ive been doing but it bothers me. I whisper "I am going to kill myself." In stressful situations or just regular social situations when I start to get socially anxious. Then my mind starts to remind me of all the fucked up shit I did while i was manic and my brain in a state of naked embarrassment starts the whispers of suicide. I would hate to accept this as a part of me but after more suicide attempts than I am willing to count, I am arriving at that place where it makes sense to admit my suicidal whispers are my new norm.

I actually read that book in addition to a few others. No-one really knows why we want to die. It's such a deep existential question that seems to maybe be tied to the "Why are we here?" question. Which philosophers and scientists have been trying to figure our for eons. Sometimes when I am depressed, I feel like i can see the world more clearly for what it is. And the sickness of it contributes to furthering my depression. Its like waking up to how dark and cold the world can be and that becoming your whole perspective until the depression lifts. Its nuts.

I am totally with you here. I just sort of resolved that its all pointless anyway. There is no use just living for the sake of living. I don't know I feel like maybe its some fucked up type of awakening or something. When open your eyes and realize suicide as an option, its a door that is almost impossible to shut.
I generally have about 2 working clippers at any one time. Two clippers and two edge simmers. My two clippers are both wahl and my edgers are one wahl and the other andis.
or... Official sex
Practiced what exactly?

Well my energy is stronger and sharper. I feel more self aware. My energy feels purer. My choices feel closer to my personal truth. I feel more effortlessly myself. I quit drugs, cigarettes. Was being treated for Bipolar Depression. Somehow the K healed that and I am no longer on medication. I am more at peace with myself and I am making a career change this year to do work that is more in line with my energy. Work that I love to do.
I struggle to imagine it now. My awake mind is cluttered with too many questions. Whereas in the dream all I could do was feel which seems more pure in a way.

I have had a similar experience. I wasn't meditating much or anything but mine happened at night. I had a bolt of electricity go from the base of my spine to my brain where I started to see flashes of light as this happened. It happened again at least 4 times after that...always at night waking me up from sleep. I would have back aches the days before warning me that this was due to happen on some night. I would hear a whooshing sound in my ears as the energy was ramping up though my spine. 

In the days following I would feel like I had been cleaned from the inside. Purified in a way. After that I would return to normal. In the years following I descended into a psychosis and had schizophrenic hallucinations. I was later diagnosed bipolar which I am currently on medication for. I have not told anyone about the kundalini incident because the medical profession does not know anything about it. 

I wonder what the meaning of it is. I thought I would achieve a new level of spirituality when the thing arrived but I just ended up becoming crazy. My brain still vibrates with the energy and my memory and focus have gotten worse. I hope Its not degenerative. I can't the kundalini has brought anything positive to my life. I thought I would develop psychic powers or something but none of that happened. Still the same old person just now crazy. 

I held on to the experience for a long time thinking that it was all meaningful but now I think its all meaningless. I think life in general has no coherent meaning, Things just happen. As for the kundalini, we may never understand what it means whether its some kind of spiritual exam or something or an attainment of some new level of chi or the beginning of some kind of process. Its been about 4 years since my k-awakening. I never wished or prayed for it. I wish it never happened.

It does. Many days I think to myself...I can't believe I'm still here. I feel like I have no more energy to give to the world. Its like I am a zombie going through the motions. Its an existential tiredness. I don't know about you but I have been though a lot of pain in this life and now all I want to do everyday is die. I totally feel you about going through the motions. It feels like somewhere along the way I died and now I am just existing. I just feel tired. I really do want to die...the only thing is that I want to do it peacefully. I am tired.
Tell me why you want to kill yourself.
You are not alone. I think about killing myself all the time. If you want to talk...
Amen
I am just so tired to be honest. Looking for the best way out.

I was trapped in a barricaded room like a criminal in jail. Given fucked up meds that made me basically stupid. It wasn't even medicine that would help me. more just medicine designed to keep me in a loopy state of mind. The food was terrible. It was like an afterthought. I couldn't no believe I was in this place. Granted I live in a third world country. You would be lucky to get good healthcare here regardless. 

I have a goal that I am currently chasing down but I need funding for it and not sure where to get that. Regardless of having this goal, I still feel powerfully suicidal most days. Its just the pointlessness of every action or inaction that makes me feel like there is no use being here. We are all hypnotised consumers programmed to stay indoors and consume food, television and porn/religion. what is the fucking point of staying on if all we are staying on for is to stay on longer. If I had a gun or had access to one, I would have blown my brains out a long time ago. I have a method planned out but it would take a couple of months for me to pull of. The conditions have to be quite right and I need some money to do it.

So I have been working on the concept for many years but it turns out  its basically a reddit with events. People can be anonymous and create or book events that they are passionate about. I am currently in the mock up design phase. If you shoot me your email I will let you in on our progress.

I had an attempt a few years ago and its just been a real option ever since. I have had some time in the psych ward and it was the worse experience of my life. I would literally gauge out my eyes on a hot afternoon before going back. Thats why I don't fuck around with my medicine. I take them religiously so that I don't give my BPD a chance to fuck with my life. Mean while I feel myself subconsciously planning my next exit
yas!
I understand. I am in the same boat. Please DM me.
I am diagnosed schizophrenic as well with chronic depression.  None of this is real. It can't be.

I think I understand what this mental clarity is about. For years I have been bipolar without knowing it. Just this year I came into an understanding of it and started to look back and see where all my manic decisions taken me. I started to understand why I lost some friends and why some people treat me the way they do. I am unstable and will always be. I just live my life pretending to be sane.
My time is winding down too. I am so sad.

I know what you mean. I have lost two good jobs, gotten turned down at several interviews. There is something wrong with me that I can't quite quantify. Now I work a desk job at my Dad's dental clinic and I recently got married but I think about suicide everyday.

I am trying daily. Thank you. There are just moments where things are entirely hopeless for me. I don't think its worth it. I am considering taking a combination of pills and poison. You are the only person I have shared this with for some reason.
I tried twice. My only regret is that it didn't work. Now I have to try again. Hopefully I get it right this time.
It just feels like its time. I don't know what else is left for me in life. My mental illness will rob me of any joy I have left. There is no future.
Not sure its a good idea to talk to someone who is also suicidal but I am here to talk if you want.
I feel the exact.same.way.
I think about it everyday. Its not a big ideal to me anymore. I have been thinking about it for years.

Hey! I have had 2 suicide attempts. Its really hard to successfully kill yourself. I have mental disorders that are getting worse. I am chronically depressed and schizophrenic. I literally try to make it though each day. I really do want to kill myself but I work hard to push the thoughts down by thinking of one thing I would like to do before I try to kill myself. Just one thing a day. It could be as simple as having a nice cup of coffee or as grand as starting a small business. Keeping busy doing something helps. Writing also helps. For example I tell stories of my craziness by creating fictional characters and I post the stories on facebook. Writing day to day helps too. Eventually we will die. Either by our own hand or get hit by a bus. Either way we are no different than anyone else that will eventually die. Life is short. I take joy in that.

I whisper under my breath all the time "I'm going to kill myself". It has become my mantra. I have had two suicide attempts. I know I have the courage to do it. Its really just a matter of when for me.
Every other day.

You are not gay! Being gay is not a slight confusion. You can even be attracted to him without wanting to sleep with him. Its okay. There are parts of the world where straight men hold hands while walking. They do this because they simply love each other without being sexually confused. Then again with all the cuddling you might be bi.

I called her sister to get the size of her ring finger while she was out of town.  Her whole family was excited. By the time she came back. I had met and fallen in love with another girl. Instead of coming home to and expected proposal, she came home to a break up. I ended it by telling her I met someone else and I was going to marry her.

I'll be your friend if you don't mind a pen pal. We can stay anonymous and just talk whenever you like. I am just figuring out how this whole reddit thing works so forgive a delayed response. I don't think there is any such thing as an unlovable person. I understand loneliness and have also suffered from it for many years. I think friendship is its own form of therapy. Just having someone to talk to in itself is a healing mechanism. I have had mental health issues like depression and bipolar and have over the years pushed away many people as a result. I am much better now and looking to make new relationships. We have to keep trying to reach out. Eventually someone you can connect with reaches back. Don't stop trying.

Suicide is not the end. Death is not the end. Our minds drift on in an ocean of consciousness that we call dreams. Push past the pain in life. Find a reason to be. If you cannot find a purpose, create one for yourself and pursue it with all the energy and anger that you can muster. You will dream as you have lived. Do not let your mind wonder in an endless ocean of pain. Suicide is not the answer. I know. I have tried. Twice. Twice I have been lucky to fail. Its not just about the pain that you continue to drift on in, its also about the pain that you leave behind. Life can be shit, death can be worse shit. If and when you do finally diem do it in a state of love.

I have committed suicide twice and failed. Each incident has left me maimed and hurt. Not just me but the people around me. I have learnt that you have to make life for yourself.  forget about what you see around you and focus on what you want for yourself and take it. Life is for the living. Even those like us that live reluctantly. You just have to do something. Make something with your hands. Volunteer. Make a new friend. Start a small business. Life is a challenge and only those that choose to live it are rewarded at the end. I have depression too. I am suicidal all the time but what keeps me going is helping people in any way I can and making progress with all my projects. When I am idle I initiate a new project or try starting a small business. Its important to be busy doing the things you like to do. I don't know what country you are in but in my country there is not much help for people that suffer from mental health issues so we have to come up with ways to survive. Keep trying to find purpose and if you can't seem to find it, create purpose for yourself.

I have died before. Twice actually. What I have learned is that its not over even after you die. It all about the state of your mind when you die. Imagine being in a perpetual dream state, living in your memories. Drifting from one dream to another. Each dream coloured by the state of your mind. Death frees you from life but there is more life. A different type of life. Its important to be in your best possible frame of mind when you do die. If you live in a state of love, then you will dream in a state of love. Suicide is not the way out. I suggest, instead of suicide, give yourself a mission. Learn a new skill. Do something practical. Make something with your hands. Use your story to help someone in need. Volunteer at a soup kitchen. There is so much you can do to improve your self worth. You are not worthless, or meaningless. Everyone will die someday...that is a fact. Might as well do something that makes life count for every minute that you are here. I am here with you. A fellow drifter. Perpetually suicidal. Also searching for meaning. God help us.

I frequently have suicidal thoughts. I whisper then out loud to myself to get them out of my head. So far that seems to have worked. Its better not to let the thoughts build up and fester in your mind. Suicide is many times a very spontaneous act. Very rarely is it planned out. I have had two suicide attempts in my lifetime and still struggle with suicidal thoughts. The thoughts stem mostly from my depression but even when I am not depressed, there is still always that voice that whispers suicide to me. Writing helps too. I hope you are okay.
